 Judgment

This is a petition filed u/s.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:

On 11-1-2022 at about 4.20 p.m. when the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-51-HG-1422 from Koppa side towards Nisarga layout side,
Harappanahalli circle, Jigani, Anekal, Bangalore, at that time, driver of the light goods vehicle bearing No.KA-51- 7566 came from Jigani side towards Bannerghatta side with high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, as a result of which petitioner sustained severe injuries and took treatment at hospital as inpatient and spent money for his treatment.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and doing fruits and vegetable business and earning Rs.30,000/-.
Due to accidental injuries, he lost the earnings and suffering from disabilities and discomforts.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.20 lakhs from the respondents.

3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.3 remained absent and placed exparte and respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsel and filed their respective written statements.

4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement contended that the petitioner was not lodged the complaint immediately, because of petitioner himself was responsible for the accident, the petitioner was ridden the motor cycle with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the Tata 709 vehicle.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

5. The respondent No.2 contended that driver of the offending vehicle has no valid and effective DL at the time of accident or letting the vehicle to a person who does not have DL is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
The offending vehicle was used in a public place without having valid permit and fitness certificate there is a violation of Section 149(2), 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and contrary to section 3 of interest Act.

The offending vehicle is not at all involved in the accident and it was intentionally implicated in Mahesha.R vs Gowrish.N on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111692626/
2 collusion with the driver, owner and other authorities to get the unlawful benefit from the insurance company by filing 2 days delayed complaint.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

6. From the above said pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the light goods vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-51-7566 on 11-1-2022 at about 4.20 pm.

At Harapanahalli circle, Harapanahalli village, Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W1 and examined two witnesses as PWs.2 and 3 and got marked Exs.P1 to P30 documents.

The respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1 and 2.
8.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:- In order to prove the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to 25 documents i.e., FIR,
complaint, spot mahazar, vehicle seizure mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, 133 MV Act notice, discharge summary, OP bill cum receipt, CT scan report, medical bills and prescriptions, aadhaar card, pass book copy, certificate, x-ray, CT scan film.
11.

It was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that there was a delay of two days in filing the complaint and the complainant has not stated the vehicle number which caused the accident in the complaint and also FIR.
Complainant only stated that one Brown colour 709 goods vehicle has caused the accident and sped away from the spot.

Learned counsel for the respondent argued that one unknown vehicle has caused the accident and it is hit and run case and in order to obtain the compensation, petitioner colluding with the respondent No.1 owner of the vehicle and IO Mahesha.
R vs Gowrish

.N on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111692626/
3 has filed the false charge sheet against the offending vehicle and hence prays to dismiss the case.
12. In the line of the defence taken by the respondent counsel, if the materials and evidence on record are perused, admittedly there was a delay of two days in filing the complaint.
The accident has been taken place on 11-1- 2022.
but the complaint has been lodged on 13-1-2022.

it is clearly stated in the Ex-P2 complaint that as the complainant Sri.Vinay has took the injured/petitioner to the hospital and he was along with the petitioner in the hospital, there was a delay in filing the complaint.
It is pertinent to note here that this fact is not at all denied by the respondent counsel.
Further on perusal of the wound certificate Ex-P6 it is clearly mentioned that alleged history of RTA on 11-1-2022 at around 4 p.m. near Harappanahalli circle, Jigani.

Further it is clear that petitioner was admitted in the medax Vijayashree hospital on 11-1-2022 as per Ex-P10 MLC.
13.

Apart from this, as per Ex-P2 admittedly it is stated that when petitioner was riding the motor cycle form Koppa towards Nisarga layout, at that time, one brown colour 709 goods vehicle came in high speed, rash and negligent manner from Jigani and hit to the motor cycle ridden by the petitioner and soon after causing the accident, sped away from the spot.

As per Ex-P3 spot mahazar conducted on 13-1-2022 it is clearly stated that the I.O. has verified the CC camara footage fixed in the Nandi bakery at the spot and found one brown goods 709 goods vehicle has caused the accident and also taken the CC footage.
Further as per Ex-P4 IO has seized the said brown colour 709 goods vehicle based on CC TV footage and found that the front glass of the said vehicle were broken.
As per Ex-P5 IMV report also the Diesel tank was damaged and left side safety guard damaged and those damages were fresh.
It is pertinent to note here that respondent No.2 has not at all denied Ex-P3 to 5 documents.
Even though respondent No.1 was examined as RW-1, RW-1 has not at all denied the involvement of the vehicle and fresh damages caused to the vehicle.

Respondent No.1 examined himself as RW-1 and filed chief affidavit evidence wherein clearly stated that when respondent No.3 Venkatesh was driving the offending vehicle, at that time, petitioner rode his motor cycle towards Koppa towards Nisarge layout in a rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden crossing the road from Koppa towards Nisarga layout, at that time, offending vehicle has touched the motor cycle and due to the incident, petitioner has sustained injuries and respondent No.3 is not responsible for the accident.
Even RW-1 clearly stated that police have collected the vehicle documents and due to the accident, goods vehicle has been damaged.
Even produced the Ex-R1 and driving licence of the driver.
Further RW-1 in his cross examination clearly admitted in the cross examination of RW-1 that -

4
14. Moreover RW-1 is not the eye witness to the accident to state that there was no rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Either of the respondents have not examined the driver of the offending vehicle.
Respondent No.3 who is an material eye witness to state about the facts and circumstances under which the accident has been taken place and to disprove the evidence of the PW-1.
Hence under such circumstances, PW-1 who is the eye witness to the accident, his evidence can be believed and relied on with regard to the rash and negligence.

15. Apart from this, on perusal of the spot mahazar, it clearly shows that spot of accident was a state highway running from Jigani towards Bannerugatta from north to south direction and width of the road was 24 feet.

Further towards the right side there was a interior road towards Koppa village on the left side, there was interior road towards Harappanahalli and spot was a circle and accident has been taken place on the extreme west side of the road.
Thus from Ex-P3 spot mahazar, it is clear that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. Thus from the evidence of RW-1, it is clear that the offending vehicle has been involved in the accident.

Even the jurisdictional police after thorough and detailed investigation filed by the charge sheet against the offending vehicle by holding that on 11-1-2022 at about 4.20 p.m. when petitioner was riding the motor cycle from Harappanahalli towards Nisarga layout, at that time, respondent No.3 drove the offending vehicle from Jigani towards Bannerughatta in high speed and rash and negligent manner and hit to the motor cycle of the petitioner and soon after the accident, driver of the offending vehicle ha snot stopped the vehicle and sped away from the spot and thereby respondent No.3 has committed the offence punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC and r/w 187 of IMV Act.
Counsel for the respondent No.2 has not placed material evidence to prove that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective and collusive.
Even not examined IO to prove that charge sheet filed by him is defective and collusive.

17. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."

Mahesha.R vs Gowrish.N on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111692626/
5 18.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.

19. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
20. ISSUE NO.2:-
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
21. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 32 years.
The petitioner has produced Ex-P20-aadhaar card which reveals that petitioner's date of birth is 1-1-1989, hence as on the date of accident, petitioner was 33 years.
The petitioner has stated that he was doing fruits and vegetable business and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from disability and deformity.
The petitioner has produced Ex-P21 and 22 bank pass book copies, but Ex-P21 and 22 does not shows what is the actual income of the petitioner.
Only on the basis of the Ex-P21 and 22, this court cannot ascertain the actual income of the petitioner.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,500/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
22. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-

As per the medical records i.e., Ex-P6- wound certificate reveals that petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., left clavicle shaft fracture, left ankle lateral malloli fracture, left ankle medial malleoli degloving injury and all injuries are described as grievous in nature and petitioner took treatment at Vijayashree multi speciality hospital Jigani from 11-1-2022 to 26-1-2022 for 16 days.
23. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW-3 who has stated that petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., degloving injury left ankle with fracture of the left lateral malleolus, left clavicle fracture with head injury and petitioner was treated at Vijayashree hospital with ORIF for the left clavicle and left fibula on 20- 1-2022 and discharged on 26-1-2022 and was on regular followup in the same hospital and fractures united.
PW-3 assessed the disability of left arm at 30%, physical disability of the left lower limb at 35%, physical disability of the left upper limb at 30% and for whole-body physical disability at 21%.
PW-3 produced Ex-P29-clinical report and Ex-P30-X- ray.

Mahesha.R vs Gowrish.N on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111692626/
6 24.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.3 has assessed the disability on the higher side.
PW-3 doctor in his cross examination admitted that personally he has not treated the petitioner.
Further PW-3 admitted that fractured bones are untied.

it Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar -vs- Ajay Kumar and Another.
25.
Considering the nature of injuries, age of petitioner, occupation of petitioner, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor
, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner was doing fruits and vegetable business, certainly has to face some difficulty and disability to carry his avocation.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 17%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 17%.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 is '16'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/-p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.5,05,920/- (Rs.15,500 X 12 X 16 X 17/100) is awarded under this head.
26. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fracture and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained left clavicle shaft fracture, left ankle lateral malloli fracture, left ankle medial malleoli degloving injury and all injuries are described as grievous in nature and petitioner took treatment at Vijayashree multi speciality hospital Jigani from 11-1-2022 to 26-1-2022 for 16 days.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony due to the injuries sustained by him on account of the accidental injuries.
The petitioner being 33 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/- under this head.

27. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the Vijayashree multi speciality hospital Jigani from 11-1-2022 to 26-1-2022 for 16 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 6 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.93,000/-
(15,500 X 6) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
28. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Sathanuru hobali,
Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara and has taken treatment at Vijayashree hospital, Bangalore for 16 days and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of treatment, the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges,
conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.

Mahesha.R vs Gowrish.N on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111692626/
7 29. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS :
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner being aged of 45 years would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Considering the age and occupation of the petitioner and the nature of injuries, a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
30. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the medical bills as per Ex-P18 for Rs.3,69,753/- and Ex-P19- prscriptions.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.3,69,753/- under the head of medical expenses.
31. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES: PW-3 has stated that petitioner require surgery for implant removal which may cost Rs.60,000/-.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding his future medical expenses.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, age and doctor evidence, this tribunal awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses.

32. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of future income : 5,05,920=00 due to disability 2P Pain & sufferings :
75,000=00 3 Loss of income during : 93,000=00 laid-up period 4A
Attendant charges, extra : 40,000=00 nutritious food &conveyance charges 5 Loss of future amenities R: 25,000=00 & happiness 1, 6

Medical expenses :
3,69,753=00 7

Future medical expenses :
50,000=00 Total 11,58,673=00
Hence petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,58,673=00.
33. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
34. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

Mahesha.R vs Gowrish.N on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111692626/
8 35.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,58,673=00 with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioner within 30 days from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 5 th day of August 2025).

Bengaluru.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
ISSUE NO.3:
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,58,673=00 with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioner within 30 days from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
